newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Three kidnap victims freed in southern Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Three kidnap victims freed in southern Philippines.

text.p: Kidnappers have released three of five government employees they abducted on the southern Philippine island of Mindanao more than a week ago, officials said on Monday.

But the kidnappers, suspected to be former Moslem rebels, are still demanding a ransom of five million pesos ($192,000) for the two others, Bimbo Sinsuat, a member of the island's semi-autonomous regional legislative assembly, told reporters.

Sinsuat headed a government team that negotiated with the kidnappers. The five, all employees of Philippine National Oil Co, were on their way to conduct geological surveys in Datu Odin Sinsuat town in Maguindanao province on January 19 when they were abducted at gunpoint.

Kidnapping for ransom has become a thriving business in the Philippines, where 241 people were abducted last year. Kidnappers collected a total of $3.8 million in ransom, a citizens' anti-crime group said.

Relatives of victims generally refuse to report the cases to authorities because of widespread suspicion that soldiers and police are themselves either members of kidnap gangs or provide protection for them.
